papers.title: WILDkCAT: Extract, retrieve, and predict enzyme turnover numbers of constraint-based metabolic models
papers.summary: Abstract Summary Accurate enzyme turnover numbers are essential for building enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models. However, collecting and curating these parameters remains a major bottleneck. Indeed, kcat values are scattered across multiple databases, reported under varying experimental conditions, and often missing for many enzymes. To address this challenge, we present WILDkCAT, a Python-based pipeline that enables the retrieval of kcat values from wild-type enzyme measured under user-specified pH and temperature ranges for a given metabolic model. The application to Escherichia coli (iML1515) and Homo sapiens (Human-GEM) models demonstrated the ability of WILDkCAT to retrieve substantial kcat coverage and its applicability across diverse genome-scale models. Availability and Implementation WILDkCAT is available at https://github.com/sysbiolux/WILDkCAT and from PyPI. WILDkCAT works on all major operating systems and computer architectures. The documentation is available at https://sysbiolux.github.io/WILDkCAT

papers.title: Odon: An ultra-fast viewer for spatial proteomics
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multiplexed spatial proteomics and spatial transcriptomics generate large, high-dimensional imaging datasets that are challenging to visualize efficiently, particularly at whole-slide and cohort scale. Visualization is an essential step for rapid detection of staining artefacts, such as protein aggregates or non-specific staining. Results Here, we present Odon, a native Rust desktop viewer designed for rapid, interactive exploration of multiplex imaging data on a standard laptop. Odon is primarily built around the OME-Zarr imaging format, and supports annotations via GeoJSON and GeoParquet, with secondary support for SpatialData, Xenium containers, and TIFF. Data can be stored locally or streamed directly from HTTP or S3-compatible object storage using viewport-driven tile loading. Odon incorporates a highly optimized rendering engine designed for viewport-driven tile loading and GPU-based compositing. In scripted benchmarks using synthetic multiplex OME-Zarr datasets, Odon showed lower peak memory use, lower affine-derived zoom-step error, and faster warm-start image loading than napari and QuPath under the tested conditions. Its GPU-based compositing pipeline also enables smooth rendering and interaction with more than 1,000,000 segmented cells. Odon further supports integrated visual analytics, including live thresholding and cell selection, and a mosaic mode for simultaneous viewing of hundreds of regions of interest in cohort and tissue microarray studies. Together, these features establish Odon as a high-performance platform for scalable visualization of spatial proteomics data. Availability Source code and compiled installers available at https://github.com/alexcoulton/odon

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 摘要：动机在于，多重空间蛋白质组学与空间转录组学所产生的数据集规模庞大、维度极高，这些数据难以高效地进行可视化分析，尤其是在全切片或大规模群体研究层面。
llm_highlights_zh: 可视化是快速识别染色伪影（如蛋白质聚集物或非特异性染色现象）的重要步骤。
在这里，我们介绍了 Odon——这款专为在标准笔记本电脑上快速、交互式地分析多模态影像数据而设计的 Rust 编程语言桌面工具。
Odon主要基于OME-Zarr成像格式构建，支持通过GeoJSON和GeoParquet进行注释记录，同时也兼容SpatialData、Xenium容器以及TIFF格式的数据文件。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
多重空间蛋白质组学与空间转录组学所产生的数据集规模庞大、维度极高，这类数据的高效可视化在整体切片或队列研究层面尤为具有挑战性。有效的可视化技术对于快速检测诸如蛋白质聚集物或非特异性染色等异常现象至关重要。  

**研究成果**  
我们推出了Odon这一专为Rust语言开发的桌面工具，它能够在标准笔记本电脑上实现对多重空间成像数据的高效、交互式分析。Odon主要基于OME-Zarr图像格式进行设计，同时支持通过GeoJSON和GeoParquet格式添加注释；此外也兼容SpatialData、Xenium容器及TIFF文件格式。数据可存储在本地，也可通过HTTP或S3兼容的对象存储服务进行流式传输，并采用视口驱动的瓦片加载机制进行读取。Odon内置了经过高度优化的渲染引擎，能够实现基于GPU的图像合成与交互操作。在针对合成生成的OME-Zarr数据集进行的测试中，Odon在内存占用、缩放精度以及图像加载速度等方面均优于napari和QuPath；其基于GPU的渲染技术还使得用户能够流畅地处理超过100万个被分割处理的细胞图像。此外，Odon还支持多种可视化分析功能，包括实时阈值设置、细胞选择操作，以及在队列研究或组织微阵列分析中同时查看数百个感兴趣区域的功能。综上所述，Odon无疑为空间蛋白质组学数据的高效可视化提供了一个高性能的平台。  

**获取方式**  
源代码及编译后的安装程序可访问以下链接获取：  
https://github.com/alexcoulton/odon

papers.title: CellPyAbility: automated image analysis for high-throughput dose-response screening
papers.summary: Abstract Summary Nuclei counting provides a low-cost, metabolic-independent alternative to ATP- or tetrazolium-based cell viability assays. However, the fragmentation of image processing, normalization, and statistical modeling across multiple software platforms hinders high-throughput adoption. We present CellPyAbility, a Python-based suite that automates image processing, dose-response fitting, and synergy analysis. It converts unedited whole-well images into publication-ready graphics in under one minute per 96-well plate on standard desktop hardware. Availability and Implementation CellPyAbility is open-source (MIT License) and available as a Python package via PyPI and Bioconda, or as a code-free application for macOS and Windows. Source code and documentation are available at https://github.com/bindralab/cellpyability and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20693745

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Summary Accurate enzyme turnover numbers are essential for building enzyme-constrained genome-scale metabolic models. However, collecting and curating these parameters remains a major bottleneck. Indeed, kcat values are scattered across multiple databases, reported under varying experimental conditions, and often missing for many enzymes. To address this challenge, we present WILDkCAT, a Python-based pipeline that enables the retrieval of kcat values from wild-type enzyme measured under user-specified pH and temperature ranges for a given metabolic model. The application to Escherichia coli (iML1515) and Homo sapiens (Human-GEM) models demonstrated the ability of WILDkCAT to retrieve substantial kcat coverage and its applicability across diverse genome-scale models.

all_papers.title: Odon: An ultra-fast viewer for spatial proteomics
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Multiplexed spatial proteomics and spatial transcriptomics generate large, high-dimensional imaging datasets that are challenging to visualize efficiently, particularly at whole-slide and cohort scale. Visualization is an essential step for rapid detection of staining artefacts, such as protein aggregates or non-specific staining. Results Here, we present Odon, a native Rust desktop viewer designed for rapid, interactive exploration of multiplex imaging data on a standard laptop. Odon is primarily built around the OME-Zarr imaging format, and supports annotations via GeoJSON and GeoParquet, with secondary support for SpatialData, Xenium containers, and TIFF. Data can be stored locally or streamed directly from HTTP or S3-compatible object storage using viewport-driven tile loading. Odon incorporates a highly optimized rendering engine designed for viewport-driven tile loading and GPU-based compositing. In scripted benchmarks using synthetic multiplex OME-Zarr datasets, Odon showed lower peak memory use, lower affine-derived zoom-step error, and faster warm-start image loading than napari and QuPath under the tested conditions. Its GPU-based compositing pipeline also enables smooth rendering and interaction with more than 1,000,000 segmented cells. Odon further supports integrated visual analytics, including live thresholding and cell selection, and a mosaic mode for simultaneous viewing of hundreds of regions of interest in cohort and tissue microarray studies. Together, these features establish Odon as a high-performance platform for scalable visualization of spatial proteomics data. Availability Source code and compiled installers available at https://github.com/alexcoulton/odon

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 摘要：动机在于，多重空间蛋白质组学与空间转录组学所产生的数据集规模庞大、维度极高，这些数据难以高效地进行可视化分析，尤其是在全切片或大规模群体研究层面。
llm_highlights_zh: 可视化是快速识别染色伪影（如蛋白质聚集物或非特异性染色现象）的重要步骤。
在这里，我们介绍了 Odon——这款专为在标准笔记本电脑上快速、交互式地分析多模态影像数据而设计的 Rust 编程语言桌面工具。
Odon主要基于OME-Zarr成像格式构建，支持通过GeoJSON和GeoParquet进行注释记录，同时也兼容SpatialData、Xenium容器以及TIFF格式的数据文件。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
多重空间蛋白质组学与空间转录组学所产生的数据集规模庞大、维度极高，这类数据的高效可视化在整体切片或队列研究层面尤为具有挑战性。有效的可视化技术对于快速检测诸如蛋白质聚集物或非特异性染色等异常现象至关重要。  

**研究成果**  
我们推出了Odon这一专为Rust语言开发的桌面工具，它能够在标准笔记本电脑上实现对多重空间成像数据的高效、交互式分析。Odon主要基于OME-Zarr图像格式进行设计，同时支持通过GeoJSON和GeoParquet格式添加注释；此外也兼容SpatialData、Xenium容器及TIFF文件格式。数据可存储在本地，也可通过HTTP或S3兼容的对象存储服务进行流式传输，并采用视口驱动的瓦片加载机制进行读取。Odon内置了经过高度优化的渲染引擎，能够实现基于GPU的图像合成与交互操作。在针对合成生成的OME-Zarr数据集进行的测试中，Odon在内存占用、缩放精度以及图像加载速度等方面均优于napari和QuPath；其基于GPU的渲染技术还使得用户能够流畅地处理超过100万个被分割处理的细胞图像。此外，Odon还支持多种可视化分析功能，包括实时阈值设置、细胞选择操作，以及在队列研究或组织微阵列分析中同时查看数百个感兴趣区域的功能。综上所述，Odon无疑为空间蛋白质组学数据的高效可视化提供了一个高性能的平台。  

**获取方式**  
源代码及编译后的安装程序可访问以下链接获取：  
https://github.com/alexcoulton/odon

all_papers.title: CellPyAbility: automated image analysis for high-throughput dose-response screening
all_papers.summary: Abstract Summary Nuclei counting provides a low-cost, metabolic-independent alternative to ATP- or tetrazolium-based cell viability assays. However, the fragmentation of image processing, normalization, and statistical modeling across multiple software platforms hinders high-throughput adoption. We present CellPyAbility, a Python-based suite that automates image processing, dose-response fitting, and synergy analysis. It converts unedited whole-well images into publication-ready graphics in under one minute per 96-well plate on standard desktop hardware. Availability and Implementation CellPyAbility is open-source (MIT License) and available as a Python package via PyPI and Bioconda, or as a code-free application for macOS and Windows. Source code and documentation are available at https://github.com/bindralab/cellpyability and on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20693745

llm_highlights_zh: 然而，图像处理、数据标准化以及统计建模功能分散在多个不同的软件平台上，这一现状阻碍了这些技术的广泛应用与高效使用。
我们推出了CellPyAbility，这是一个基于Python开发的工具包，能够自动完成图像处理、剂量-反应关系分析以及协同作用研究。
在标准的桌面硬件上，它每分钟能够将一个96孔板中未经处理的整孔图像转换为适合发表的图形格式。
